items.title: Sub-Part 27, the Final Sub-Part: The Five Marks That Forge a Genuinely Virtuous Practitioner

items.zh: 於過去無戀，不悕求未來，現在諸法中，處處遍觀察，智者所增長，無奪亦無動。
items.en: No longing for the past, no craving for the future, observing thoroughly, everywhere, the phenomena of the present — this is what the wise cultivate and increase: unseizable, and unshakeable.

items.zh: 此是造賢善頌。謂如有一，於佛所證法毘奈耶獲得淨信，以正信心棄捨家法，趣於非家。由五種相修行梵行，令善清淨。謂能捨離居家諸行，無所顧戀；亦不緣彼心生追戀，還起染著。是名初相。又於現法利養恭敬未來種類所有諸行，不生悕望；亦不願求當來人天所有諸行，修行梵行。是第二相。又於現在五取蘊攝色等諸法及彼安立，能正觀察。又於現法及當來世諸身惡行及惡果報，謂我於身不應發起所有惡行，廣說如經，乃至應斷身諸惡行，修身善行。語意善行，當知亦爾。又於色等諸蘊，能隨觀察去來今世，皆是無常。無常故苦；苦故無我；由無我故，於彼一切不執我所，乃至於彼不執為我。如是如實正慧觀察。是第三相。又依初法毘鉢舍那，諸根成熟，福德、智慧二種資糧，於當來世通達增長，非諸王等所能劫奪。是第四相。又依第二法毘鉢舍那，於現法中涅槃功德能善增長，非諸煩惱及隨煩惱所能傾動。是第五相。由此五相，修行梵行，令善清淨。若依如是一日一夜，亦為賢善、第一賢善。當知超度此餘一切所有梵行。復次，今當略辯上所說義。謂薄伽梵此中略示，於善說法毘奈耶中所修梵行、於一切相皆善清淨，不與他共。當知是名此中略義。嗢拕南曰：惡、說、貪、流、怖、類、與、池、流、貪、作、劬勞、得義、論議十四種。
items.en: This is the verse on making [a night] auspicious. Someone gains pure faith in the Dharma and Vinaya realised by the Buddha, and with a mind of right faith gives up household life and goes forth into homelessness. In five ways they practise the holy life and make it thoroughly pure. They are able to give up the activities of household life without regret, nor does their mind, taking those activities as its object, give rise to longing and turn again to attachment. This is called the first aspect. Again, they practise the holy life without hoping for the gain and honour of the present life or for activities of a future kind, and without wishing for any activities among humans and gods in the future. This is the second aspect. Again, they are able to observe rightly the present phenomena, form and the rest included in the five aggregates of clinging, and how they are established. Again, regarding bad bodily conduct and its bad results here and now and in the future, [they reflect]: 'I should not engage in any bad bodily conduct,' and so on at length as in the sutra, up to: 'one should abandon bad bodily conduct and cultivate good bodily conduct.' Good verbal and mental conduct should be understood likewise. Again, they are able to observe that the aggregates of form and the rest, in past, future and present, are all impermanent. Being impermanent, they are suffering; being suffering, they are not-self; because they are not-self, they do not grasp any of them as mine, up to not grasping them as self. Thus they observe with right wisdom as it really is. This is the third aspect. Again, relying on the first kind of insight into phenomena, their faculties ripen, and their two stores of merit and wisdom will be penetrated and increased in the future, and cannot be plundered by kings and the like. This is the fourth aspect. Again, relying on the second kind of insight into phenomena, they are able to increase well, here and now, the virtues of nirvana, which cannot be shaken by the afflictions and secondary afflictions. This is the fifth aspect. In these five ways they practise the holy life and make it thoroughly pure. Even if one relies on this for a single day and night, it is auspicious, the foremost of the auspicious. It should be understood that this surpasses all other kinds of holy life. Further, the meaning of what was said above will now be briefly set out. In this verse the Blessed One briefly shows that the holy life cultivated in the well-proclaimed Dharma and Vinaya is thoroughly pure in every aspect and is not shared with others. It should be understood that this is the summary meaning here. The summary verse says: Evil, speech, greed, streams, fear, kinds, and pool; streams, greed, making, toil, gaining the meaning, and discussion: fourteen kinds.

blocks.text: A short final day. One verse, with an explanation missing from Ru-Yi's translation (the English column gives our own), closes the Stage Attained Through Reflection. Tomorrow begins the twelfth stage, the **Stage Attained Through Cultivation** (修所成地).
"No longing for the past, no craving for the future, observing thoroughly, everywhere, the phenomena of the present: this is what the wise cultivate and increase: unseizable and unshakeable."

One who goes forth with faith lives the holy life purely through five marks: 1. **Not longing for the past:** having left home, one does not look back with attachment. Master Cháng Bǎi: let go of the beloved household without lingering. 2. **Not craving the future:** one does not practise for gain and honour, nor for future human or heavenly pleasures. Venerable Miào Jìng: those riches are still desire. 3. **Observing the present:** one examines the five aggregates of clinging; resolves to give up bodily, verbal, and mental misconduct; and sees all aggregates, past, future, present, as impermanent, therefore suffering, therefore not-self, and so not "mine" or "I". 4. **Unseizable:** through the first insight, merit and wisdom grow for the future, which no king can seize. 5. **Unshakeable:** through the second insight, the qualities of nirvāṇa grow now, unmoved by any affliction. Master Cháng Bǎi: stream-entry is "unseizable"; arhatship, "unshakeable".
Living this way for even "one day and one night" is virtuous, "the foremost virtue", surpassing every other kind of holy life.
A summary verse then lists the fourteen topics of the essential-body verses: evil, speech, greed, flood, fear, the classes, giving, the spring, the flood, greed, work, toil, benefit, and discussion.

subs.head: Looking back on the Stage of Reflection

blocks.text: Venerable Miào Jìng: the Stage of Reflection is complete here. It began by sorting what exists from what does not, moved to the verses on non-self, then to the three trainings, and ended with dozens of verses on daily life. Reflection, in this treatise, is never only intellectual: every verse turns back on how one lives.

quiz.q: What does the final verse say the wise do towards the past, the future, and the present?
options: recall the past, plan the future
no longing for the past, no craving for the future, thoroughly observing present phenomena — unseizable and unshakeable
quiz.why: "No longing for the past, no craving for the future, observing thoroughly, everywhere, the phenomena of the present — this is what the wise cultivate and increase: unseizable, and unshakeable." Master Cháng Bǎi: attaining stream-entry is "unseizable," and arhatship "unshakeable."

quiz.q: How do the two masters explain "no longing for the past"?
options: Cháng Bǎi: after going forth, let go of the beloved household; Miào Jìng frankly notes that a new monastic may last two weeks before missing home
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: after going forth, one must let go of the beloved household of the past, without lingering attachment. Venerable Miào Jìng: but after going forth, at most for two weeks the mind does not cling; after two weeks one may still miss home.

quiz.q: The note explains "no craving for the future" only as not seeking future gain and fame. What further layer does Venerable Miào Jìng add?
options: even the riches of future human or heavenly rebirth are desire — one does not practise for them
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: all the riches of future human and heavenly births are still desire; one does not practise the holy life for them. The treatise's second mark includes not wishing for future human or divine existence, which the note omits. Master Cháng Bǎi: still hoping for gain and honour is like eating again what one has vomited.

quiz.q: How does Master Cháng Bǎi match "unseizable and unshakeable" to the fruits?
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: further attaining stream-entry is called unseizable; up to attaining arhatship is called unshakeable. Venerable Miào Jìng: stream-entry on the path of seeing is the first insight into the Dharma.

quiz.q: f19's close says the transition from reflection to cultivation is deferred to fascicle 20. What does Venerable Miào Jìng say at the end of this fascicle?
options: the Ground of Reflection is complete here — the Ground of Cultivation is next
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: the Ground of What Is Attained Through Reflection is complete here. The fourteen topics of the essential-body verses end in this fascicle, and with them the ground; f19's closing statement is misleading.
